doc.title: Eddie Bert interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Growing up in the Bronx and Mount Vernon; getting a Wurlitzer trombone
summary: No musical family; school band, alto horn, bass drum, then a broken-umbrella trombone and a cheap Wurlitzer horn.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Yeah. Long time. Did you come from a musical background, your family?
What made you gravitate — and was trombone your first instrument?

Not really. You see I grew up in the Bronx. Then when I was ten I moved to Mount Vernon. And in the Bronx they didn’t have any band so I didn’t know where that radio, the radio stuff came from. I heard the radio and I heard music but I didn’t know anything about it. So then when I got to Mount Vernon they had a band in the school, in the elementary school. And the teacher said, “here, try this trumpet.” So I played the trumpet. And she said yeah, you’d be a good trumpet player, tell your father to get you a horn. Nothing. So I had to take what was there. And they had an E flat alto horn. And you don’t do too much with that. When the tuba goes oomph, you go pah. Oomph-pah, oomph-pah, © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

oomph. And that got kind of boring. So one day we were playing a concert in one of the schools and we were playing the “Skater’s Waltz,” and the drummer couldn’t play three- four. So I said let me play that. Because I had some friends in the drum section you know. So anyway I started playing bass drum and we were right in back of the trombones. And they had these counter melodies in the marches and stuff like that. And I said yeah, I like that. So I had a broken umbrella. And, you know the part that goes up? So I did that, and I had a razzer. You know what a razzer is?

One of those big rubber things brrumph, brrumpt, brrumph. So I’d walk down the street going like that. So finally my father says what are you doing? I says playing trombone. But it isn’t a trombone. I said yeah but I don’t have one. So he finally got me one of these stupid, it was like what we call a pea shooter. It was made by Wurlitzer. And it was a terrible horn but it was a horn. So I played it for a little bit.
It was a trombone but just a lousy one?
Yeah. But then after about a year he bought me a horn. So that’s how I started.
That’s a great story. Wouldn’t it be cool to have a picture of you going down the street with that umbrella. You know it’s funny too, a lot of guys, did you say it was a Sears trombone?
They made pianos but I guess they made a few instruments.
Sure. A lot of those early instruments came from them, and the catalogue, and cost five or six dollars.
